blocks.text: Answer synthesis prompting goes beyond the multi-document handling covered in the previous topic to focus specifically on how the final answer itself gets constructed, combining information from several sources into one coherent, well organized response rather than a list of what each source individually said.

This topic covers the difference between simple extraction and genuine synthesis, organizing a combined answer by theme rather than by source, balancing comprehensiveness with conciseness, and keeping a synthesized answer grounded in its sources even as it becomes more integrated.
1. What Answer Synthesis Means

blocks.alt: Building on multi-document prompting, answer synthesis prompting produces one coherent combined answer

blocks.text: Answer synthesis is the process of combining information from multiple retrieved sources into a single, coherent answer, rather than simply presenting each source contribution separately, this is the specific output-side skill the previous topic input-side handling sets up.
2. Synthesis vs Simple Extraction

blocks.alt: Extraction lists what each source individually says, synthesis produces one combined, coherent answer

blocks.text: A response that says "Document A states X, Document B states Y, Document C states Z" is extraction, technically accurate but not genuinely useful as a single answer, synthesis instead weaves that same information into "the evidence indicates X, with additional considerations around Y and Z," a more genuinely readable and useful response.

code.content:
prompt = (
    "Synthesize the information from all provided documents into a single, "
    "coherent answer. Do not simply list what each document says separately, "
    "combine the relevant information into one clear response."
)

blocks.text: 3. Organizing by Theme, Not by Source

blocks.alt: Organizing by source is compared against organizing by theme, combined across sources

blocks.text: A synthesized answer generally reads better organized around the actual themes or aspects of the question, rather than mechanically walking through each source one at a time, this connects to the structured prompting technique covered in an earlier module, applied here to organize the output around content rather than source.

blocks.text: 4. Balancing Comprehensiveness With Conciseness

blocks.alt: A too terse synthesis drops relevant detail, a too verbose one includes everything regardless of relevance, a balanced synthesis sits between

blocks.text: An overly terse synthesis risks dropping genuinely relevant detail found across the sources, an overly verbose one includes every detail regardless of actual relevance to the question, a well calibrated synthesis includes what genuinely matters for answering the actual question and leaves out what does not.
5. Synthesizing Without Losing Grounding

blocks.alt: A synthesized claim still traces back to specific sources

blocks.text: This connects directly back to the grounding techniques covered earlier in this module, combining information into a more fluent, integrated answer should not come at the cost of losing traceability, a well synthesized answer can still be checked against its underlying sources, even though it reads as one unified response rather than a list of separate excerpts.

blocks.title: Synthesis and grounding are not in tension, done well
blocks.content: It is entirely possible to write a fluent, well organized synthesized answer that still cites its sources accurately, the two goals only conflict when synthesis is done carelessly, blending claims together so thoroughly that their original source becomes untraceable.

blocks.text: 6. A Worked Synthesis Example

Given three retrieved excerpts about a product feature, one describing its function, one describing a limitation, and one describing a workaround, a well synthesized answer weaves these into a single coherent explanation, rather than three separate paragraphs each starting with which document it came from.
7. When Synthesis Should Preserve Distinct Perspectives

blocks.alt: When sources agree, a consensus view emerges, when sources genuinely differ, distinct perspectives get preserved

blocks.text: This connects directly to the conflict handling covered in the previous topic, synthesis works well for combining agreeing information into one consensus view, but when sources genuinely offer different perspectives or conflicting information, synthesis should preserve that distinction explicitly rather than incorrectly blending genuinely different viewpoints into one falsely unified answer.
8. Testing Synthesis Quality

blocks.alt: A synthesis quality check confirms the answer is coherent and accurate

blocks.text: Evaluating a synthesized answer means checking two things together, does it read as a coherent, well organized response, and does every claim within it still trace back accurately to the actual source material, a synthesis that reads beautifully but drifts from its sources has failed just as much as one that is accurate but disjointed.
9. Answer Synthesis and the Rest of This Module

This topic completes the output-side counterpart to multi-document prompting, the final topic in this module, source attribution, covers how to properly cite the sources behind a synthesized answer, closing the loop between combining information fluently and still making it verifiable.
Worked Example

A developer building a research summarization tool initially produces answers that read as three disconnected paragraphs, one per source document, awkward and repetitive when the sources cover overlapping ground.

Adding an explicit synthesis instruction, asking the model to organize its answer around the actual themes present in the question rather than walking through each source separately, produces a noticeably more readable, coherent response, while a grounding check confirms every claim in the new synthesized version still traces back correctly to its original source.
Common Mistakes

items: Producing a response organized by source, "Document A says, Document B says," instead of genuinely synthesized around the actual question
Losing traceability to source material while synthesizing information into a more fluent answer
Blending genuinely different perspectives from sources into one falsely unified claim instead of preserving the distinction
Producing an overly verbose synthesis that includes every detail regardless of actual relevance to the question asked

blocks.text: Practice

Take three short simulated source excerpts covering different but related aspects of a topic, write a prompt instructing genuine synthesis organized by theme rather than by source, and check whether the resulting answer both reads coherently and remains traceable back to its underlying sources.
Key Takeaway

Answer synthesis combines information from multiple sources into one coherent, theme organized answer rather than a list of separate source excerpts, balancing comprehensiveness with conciseness, and it should preserve grounding and distinct perspectives where sources genuinely differ, rather than blending everything into a falsely unified response.
